cover.title: Freakonomics
cover.author: Steven D. Levitt & Stephen J. Dubner

segments.text: A daycare was fed up with parents picking their kids up late, so they started charging a small fine. Late pickups didn't fall. They doubled.
Before the fine, being late meant guilt. You'd stranded a tired teacher. The fine swapped that guilt for a price, and a cheap one. Parents just bought the right to be late.
That's the trap. An incentive doesn't only add a cost. It can quietly rewrite what the whole thing means.
